steps.message:
# Ship the approved change tickets

Change requests are tickets in the `tickets` service. Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. Operating procedures, including the release runbook and any change freezes, are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

Ship every change ticket that is ready, following the current release runbook and the change freezes in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds archived and ended versions of some procedures; follow the current ones. Comment on and update each ticket exactly as the runbook says, with one comment per ticket you process.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the MCP tools for the three services.

If the build fails, comment \\\"build failed\\\" on the ticket and set it to pending.\\n2. Deploy the build to staging, unless it is already the live release there.\\n3. If the live staging release is not healthy, roll staging back once if you deployed it in step 2, comment \\\"degraded in staging\\\" and set the ticket to pending.\\n4. Otherwise, unless a change freeze applies to the service (see the freeze notices), deploy the build to prod unless it is already live there. Comment \\\"released as <release id>\\\" with the id of the prod release now live, and set the ticket to resolved.\\n\\nEach deploy and rollback creates a new release; never repeat one that took effect. Leave tickets that are not ready untouched.\\n\"}"}]}}

steps.message:
I processed all eight ready change tickets (701–708) under the current runbook and the payments freeze, and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. I didn't re-check deploy or ticket state after the final updates. I relied on each call's returned result.

| Ticket | Service | Outcome | Comment | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 701 | auth-api | Build was already live in staging and healthy, so I deployed to prod only (r-90) | released as r-90 | resolved |
| 702 | billing-api | Deployed to staging, held back from prod by the payments freeze | held for freeze | pending |
| 703 | cart-svc | Staging healthy, prod r-91 | released as r-91 | resolved |
| 704 | notify-worker | Staging was degraded, so I rolled it back once (r-89) | degraded in staging | pending |
| 705 | orders-api | Staging healthy, prod r-92 | released as r-92 | resolved |
| 706 | search-api | Build b-53 failed | build failed | pending |
| 707 | ledger-api | Deployed to staging, held back from prod by the payments freeze | held for freeze | pending |
| 708 | pricing-svc | Staging healthy, prod r-93 | released as r-93 | resolved |

- **Freeze:** the payments freeze runs 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-16 and covers billing-api and ledger-api. I ignored the ended search freeze and the archived 2025 runbook.
- **Skipped tickets:** 709 has no `approved` label and 710 is already pending. I left both untouched, along with the non-change tickets.

Each ticket got exactly one comment.
